threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to the nearest tube station; locals know it's all about the bus or Overground here.
Last night on the 196, a guy was literally trying to sell off-brand energy drinks like they were vintage wine. Oddly charming.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a full suit pull out a saxophone in the U-Bahn, just playing for the sheer joy of it. That’s Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 3 AM and find a street musician jamming with a saxophone right beside you. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local would know not to stand too close to the BART doors at Civic Center when they hear that loud bang today. Avoided chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing a full-sized piano on the 5 bus yesterday. He was nailing every note, while passengers just stared, some smiling, others filming.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the Gaudí sights. But if you’re not in a local bar by 10 PM, you’re missing the real vibe—kids playing on streets, people sharing wine.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their overzealous excitement for the local 'vermut' bars, while the locals casually switch to beer.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the bus will come on time because of that silly timetable. Welcome to the real world, mate—it's more of a guideline.
Caught a whiff of plantain being cooked on the 3 bus last night—made the long wait feel like a home-cooked dinner in the middle of Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a toddler in a dinosaur costume playing in front of a kebab shop on a Saturday afternoon. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain will you find techno parties in abandoned buildings next to grandma's fruit stand. It's a wild mash-up of old and new.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their indifference to the BART delays; they know it’s just Tuesday and have already planned around it.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo eating a burrito on the 22 Fillmore. Only in SF do fancy and casual collide like that.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think Gràcia is just about Gaudí. They miss the hidden squares where locals sip on vermut and talk about football like it’s life or death.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their over-enthusiastic attempts to try every tapas bar on the block in one weekend. Locals know it’s a marathon, not a sprint.
